items.title: About Me
items.text:
I am a lifelong learner with a lot of drive and excitement for my future in the professional world. I am quick to learn and enjoy the challenge of solving the problem at hand.

I'm currently a Ph.D. student in the Magnetic & Medical Robotics Lab at the University of Utah, under Dr. Jake J. Abbott.

The working title of my dissertation is "Linear Modeling and Model-based Manipulation of Conductive Nonmagnetic Objects Using Magnetic Induction."

items.title: Formula Sheets
items.text:
In studying for exams, I have always known I was prepared once I was happy with my formula sheet. Fortunately, I leared about \(\LaTeX\) early on (i.e., Sophmore Dynamics), and preppaing a formula sheet felt the perfect time to learn. Since then, my typesetting abilities have grown with every formula sheet I made; a skill that I deeply value.

So here is a sampling of what I've done over the years! They are presented roughly in chronological order. Although some of the graphics were made by me, there are also screenshots from textbooks as well (e.g., the many tables in Heat Transfer), for which I claim no credit. I do however claim credit for every falsehood and typo included.

items.title: German Whispers
items.text:
In variant Sudoku, i.e., Sudoku with rules extending beyond the overlapping sets of 1-9, a popular rule that is used is called a German Whisper Line. On this line, typically colored green, adjacent digits along the line must differ in value by at least five. When I was first learning how this rule, I found it very difficult to keep the options for each digits straight. So, I made this mathematical graph to remind myself of the rules. The nodes are the normal Sudoku digits, and edges are present between digits that could be adjacent on the German Whisper Line.

Made with draw.io
